fd3e23.conditions: Only one pool holds the requested k point for each spin, so each (tag, spin) pair has exactly one sender and the wildcard receives cannot take a different message
fd3e23.reasoning: The only wildcard receives on this path are in elph_prt (PHonon/PH/elphon.f90:1508-1513). The ionode receives with MPI_ANY_SOURCE, but every receive names a specific tag: 4*nproc+ispn-1 (12/13) for el_ph_mat and 6*nproc+ispn-1 (18/19) for the two et messages. Each spin's k point appears once in the k list, so exactly one pool root sends each spin's messages. The two et sends that share a tag come from the same source, so non-overtaking keeps them in order. The ionode posts its receives in the order spin1 (12,18,18) then spin2 (13,19,19), which is the order any sender issues them. If the senders are on different ranks, a sender in rendezvous mode only waits for a receive that is posted later; no cycle forms, so buffering cannot cause a deadlock. elph_prt runs once (one q). With one process per pool, the FFT scatters do no point-to-point, and every other communication goes through QE's mp wrappers, which use explicit sources.
